en: 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: I saw Jabir ibn 'Abdullah swearing by Allah that Ibn Sa'id was the Dajjal. So I said: 'Do you swear by Allah?' He said: 'Indeed, I heard 'Umar swearing to that in the presence of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) did not object to it.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, that Ibn Sayyad asked the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about the soil of Paradise, so he said: 'Fine white flour, pure musk.'

Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us: Bishr—meaning Ibn Mufaddal—narrated to us, from Abu Maslamah, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to Ibn Sa'id: 'What is the soil of Paradise?' He said: 'Fine white flour, musk, O Abu al-Qasim.' He said: 'You have spoken the truth.'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Salim ibn Nuh narrated to us: Al-Jurayri informed me, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: We set out as pilgrims for Hajj or 'Umrah, and Ibn Sa'id was with us. He said: We halted at a station, and the people dispersed, leaving only me and him. I felt an intense dread of him because of what was being said about him. He said: He brought his luggage and placed it with my luggage. So I said: 'The heat is intense; why not place it under that tree?' He said: So he did so. He said: Then a flock of sheep appeared to us, so he went and brought a large cup of milk and said: 'Drink, O Abu Sa'id.' I said: 'The heat is intense, and the milk is warm,' though my only reason was that I disliked drinking from his hand—or he said: taking from his hand. So he said: 'O Abu Sa'id! I was on the verge of taking a rope, tying it to a tree, and strangling myself because of what the people say to me! O Abu Sa'id, if the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) remains hidden to anyone, it is not hidden to you, O assembly of the Ansar! Are you not among the most knowledgeable of people regarding the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)? Did not the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "He is a disbeliever," while I am a Muslim? Did not the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "He is sterile and will have no children," whereas I have left my child behind in Medina? Did not the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "He will not enter Medina nor Mecca," whereas I have come from Medina and am heading to Mecca?' Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: Until I was almost ready to accept his excuse. Then he said: 'As for me, by Allah, I certainly know him, I know where he was born, and where he is right now!' He said: I said to him: 'May you perish for the rest of the day!'

Yahya ibn Habib and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, both saying: Mu'tamir narrated to us, saying: I heard my father narrating from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: Ibn Sa'id said to me—and I felt a sense of embarrassment toward him: 'I might excuse the people, but what is between me and you, O companions of Muhammad? Did not the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "He is a Jew," while I have embraced Islam? And he said: "And he will have no children," while I have had a child born to me? And he said: "Indeed, Allah has forbidden Mecca to him," while I have performed Hajj?' He said: He kept on until his words almost influenced me. He said: Then it was said to him: 'As for me, by Allah, I certainly know where he is right now, and I know his father and his mother.' He said: And it was said to him: 'Would it please you to be that man?' He said: He replied: 'If it were offered to me, I would not dislike it.'

'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, both saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us: Dawud narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: I accompanied Ibn Sa'id to Mecca, and he said to me: 'What trouble I have encountered from the people! They claim that I am the Dajjal. Did you not hear the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "He will have no children born to him"?' He said: I said: 'Yes indeed.' He said: 'Yet a child has been born to me. And did you not hear the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "He will not enter Medina nor Mecca"?' I said: 'Yes indeed.' He said: 'Yet I was born in Medina, and here I am heading for Mecca!' He said: Then at the end of his speech he said to me: 'As for me, by Allah, I certainly know where he was born, his place, and where he is.' He said: So he confounded me.

Yahya ibn Habib and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, both saying: Mu'tamir narrated to us, saying: I heard my father say: Abu Nadrah narrated to us, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: The Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) met Ibn Sa'id while Abu Bakr and 'Umar were with him, and Ibn Sa'id was with the boys... and he mentioned the like of the hadith of al-Jurayri.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Salim ibn Nuh narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), Abu Bakr, and 'Umar met him in one of the pathways of Medina, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: 'Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Do you testify that I am the messenger of Allah?' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'I believe in Allah, His angels, and His Books. What do you see?' He said: 'I see a throne upon the water.' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'You see the throne of Iblis upon the sea. And what else do you see?' He said: 'I see two truthful ones and a liar, or two liars and a truthful one.' So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'He has been confounded; leave him.'

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Kurayb's; Ibn Numayr said: 'narrated to us', and the other two said: 'informed us'—Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from 'Abdullah, who said: We were walking with the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he passed by Ibn Sayyad. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: 'I have concealed something for you.' He said: 'Dukh.' So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Be off with you! You will never exceed your station!' Thereupon 'Umar said: 'O Messenger of Allah, let me strike his neck!' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Leave him, for if he is the one you fear, you will not be able to kill him.'

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is 'Uthman's; Ishaq said: 'informed us', and 'Uthman said: 'narrated to us'—Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abdullah, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and we passed by some boys among whom was Ibn Sayyad. The boys fled while Ibn Sayyad remained seated, and it seemed that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) disliked that. So the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: 'May your hands be covered in dust! Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'No, rather you should testify that I am the messenger of Allah!' So 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: 'Leave me, O Messenger of Allah, to kill him!' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'If he is the one you think, you will never be able to kill him.'

Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to me, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, with this chain of narration, the like of it. Simak said: And I heard my brother saying: Jabir said: 'So beware of them.'

Yahya ibn Yahya and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—Yahya said: 'informed us', and Abu Bakr said: 'narrated to us'—Abu al-Ahwas [H]; and Abu Kamil al-Jahdari narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, both from Simak, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: 'Indeed, shortly before the Hour there will be great liars.' And he added in the hadith of Abu al-Ahwas: He said: I said to him, 'Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?' He said: 'Yes.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Ya'qub—meaning Ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman—narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Hour will not be established until the Muslims fight the Jews and the Muslims kill them, until the Jew hides behind rocks and trees, and the rock or tree will say: "O Muslim, O servant of Allah, this is a Jew behind me, so come and kill him!"—except the gharqad tree, for indeed it is among the trees of the Jews.'

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab: Salim ibn 'Abdullah narrated to me that 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar informed him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Jews will fight you and you will be given dominance over them, until the stone will say: "O Muslim, this is a Jew behind me, so kill him!"'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us: 'Umar ibn Hamzah informed me, saying: I heard Salim saying: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar informed us that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'You and the Jews will fight one another until the stone will say: "O Muslim, this is a Jew behind me, come and kill him!"'

And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated it to us, both saying: Yahya narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah, with this chain of narration, and he said in his hadith: '"This is a Jew behind me."'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'You will surely fight the Jews and you will surely kill them, until the stone will say: "O Muslim, this is a Jew, so come and kill him!"'
Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to me: Bishr ibn 'Umar az-Zahrani narrated to us: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to me: Thawr ibn Zayd ad-Dili narrated to us, in this chain of narration, the like of it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn Muhammad—narrated to us, from Thawr—and he is Ibn Zayd ad-Dili—from Abu al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Have you heard of a city one side of which is on land and one side of which is in the sea?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'The Hour will not be established until 70,000 of the descendants of Ishaq invade it. When they reach it, they will dismount, yet they will not fight with weapons nor shoot an arrow; they will say: "La ilaha illallah, wallahu akbar", and one of its two sides will fall.' Thawr said: I do not know it except that he said: 'the one that is in the sea. Then they will say a second time: "La ilaha illallah, wallahu akbar," and its other side will fall. Then they will say a third time: "La ilaha illallah, wallahu akbar," and a passage will be opened for them, so they will enter it and take spoils. While they are dividing the spoils, a caller will come crying out: "The Dajjal has emerged!" So they will leave everything and return.'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Samurah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)... with the meaning of the hadith of Abu 'Awanah.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Abu Kamil al-Jahdari narrated to us, both saying: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: 'A troop from among the Muslims—or from among the believers—will surely conquer the treasure of the dynasty of Chosroes which is in the White Palace.' Qutaybah said: 'from among the Muslims,' and did not doubt.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'When Chosroes perishes, there will be no Chosroes after him...' and he mentioned the exact like of the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)... and he mentioned a number of hadiths among which was that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Chosroes has perished, and there will be no Chosroes after him; and Caesar will surely perish, and there will be no Caesar after him; and their treasures will surely be divided in the cause of Allah.'

'Amr an-Naqid and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Abi 'Umar's—both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Chosroes has died, and there will be no Chosroes after him; and when Caesar perishes, there will be no Caesar after him. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, their treasures will surely be spent in the cause of Allah.' And Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me [H]; and Ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me from 'Abd ar-Razzaq: Ma'mar informed us; both of them from az-Zuhri, with the chain of narration of Sufyan and the meaning of his hadith.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu at-Tayyah, who said: I heard Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'This clan of Quraysh will destroy my Ummah.' They said: 'What do you command us?' He said: 'If only people would keep away from them!' And Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ad-Dawraqi and Ahmad ibn 'Uthman an-Nawfali narrated to us, both saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, in this chain of narration, with its meaning.

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn, from al-Hasan, from his mother, from Umm Salamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The rebellious group will kill 'Ammar.'

And Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith informed us: Shu'bah narrated to us: Khalid al-Hadhdha' narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan and al-Hasan, from their mother, from Umm Salamah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Jabalah narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us [H]; and 'Uqbah ibn Mukram al-'Ammi and Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated to us—'Uqbah said: 'narrated to us', and Abu Bakr said: 'informed us'—Ghundar narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Khalid narrating from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan, from his mother, from Umm Salamah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to 'Ammar: 'The rebellious group will kill you.'

Muhammad ibn Mu'adh ibn 'Abbad al-'Anbari and Huraym ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, both saying: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us [H]; and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Ishaq ibn Mansur, Mahmud ibn Ghaylan, and Muhammad ibn Qudamah narrated to us, saying: An-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us; both of them from Shu'bah, from Abu Maslamah, with this chain of narration, the like of it, except that in the hadith of an-Nadr it is: 'There informed me one who is better than me: Abu Qatadah.' And in the hadith of Khalid ibn al-Harith he said: 'I think he meant Abu Qatadah.' And in the hadith of Khalid he said: 'and he said: "Waysa"' or he said: '"O Waysa Ibn Sumayyah!"'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Maslamah, who said: I heard Abu Nadrah narrating from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: There informed me one who is better than me that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to 'Ammar when he began digging the trench, and he wiped his head, saying: 'Alas, Ibn Sumayyah! A rebellious group will kill you.'
